Carbon comes in several different solid forms, called allotropes. The most familiar are diamond and graphite. Diamond is the hardest known natural material. Graphite is soft and is used in pencils and as a lubricant. Other allotropes include amorphous carbon, fullerenes, and carbon nanotubes. Carbon is the fourth most common element in the universe by mass. On Earth, carbon is found in the air as carbon dioxide gas, in plants and animals, in coal and oil, and in limestone rock. All known forms of life contain carbon. The study of carbon-based molecules is called organic chemistry. Carbon dating is a method used to find the age of old objects that once contained living material. It measures small amounts of a special form of carbon called carbon-fourteen.
